title: PureCycle Announces Multi-Year Feedstock Agreement with WM for Nearly 25 Million Pounds of Polypropylene Per Year
summary: PureCycle and WM are linking two critical parts of the polypropylene recycling chain by signing a multi-year feedstock agreement.
body_markdown:
##### Agreement with North America’s Largest Recycler Secures Recycled Polypropylene Supply and Will Help Build on Shared Circularity Work with Brands


**ORLANDO, Fla.** –[PureCycle Technologies, Inc.](https://www.purecycle.com/) (Nasdaq: PCT), a U.S.-based company revolutionizing plastic recycling, today announced a long-term feedstock agreement with WM, North America’s leading environmental solutions provider and largest recycler. WM will supply PureCycle with nearly 25 million pounds per year of waste polypropylene (PP) bales over a multi-year period beginning in November 2026.


The agreement links two parts of the PP recycling chain. WM collects and sorts recyclables at scale, and PureCycle turns post-consumer PP into PureFive® resin. Together they are working to bring more recycled PP back into the market as new packaging.


The agreement builds on WM’s recent investment in its recycling network. WM has increased the amount of PP it recycles by 250% since 2019. In November 2025, WM added plastic cups made of polypropylene, along with paper to-go cups, to its universal list of accepted recyclable materials, so more residents across the U.S. can recycle these cups curbside. WM has also invested in advanced sorting technology at many of its facilities, with all of its single-stream recycling facilities now accepting paper and PP cups.


“Polypropylene is in many of the products people use every day, and making it truly circular requires strong end markets for what is recycled and businesses and brands committed to using domestic recycled content,” said Ryan Nordt, executive director, recycling, WM. “We’re on track to increase the amount of polypropylene we recycle by approximately 250% since 2019, and our agreement with PureCycle is a big step toward putting more of that material back to work.”


“WM’s investment in collecting and sorting polypropylene is helping make more material available to be recycled into new products,” said Chris Talarek, VP of Feedstock at PureCycle. “This agreement gives us a long-term supply of recycled PP from the largest recycler in North America, and it reflects what we are working to build together: a path for PP that goes from the recycling bin, to WM’s facilities, to PureFive® resin, and back into products that consumers use every day.”


The two companies are also continuing to work together on circularity programs with brands. That work has already begun with efforts at sports stadiums, where stadium recyclables are collected and sorted at WM, sent to PureCycle’s dissolution recycling facility and then the PureFive® resin is used by souvenir cup manufacturers for stadiums across the country. The companies see opportunities to extend this work into other high-volume settings, including quick service restaurants and convenience stores, where PP cups are widely used and increasingly accepted in curbside recycling.


PureCycle’s physical, dissolution recycling process transforms post-consumer polypropylene into PureFive® resin by removing color, odor, additives and other impurities from the plastic. The resin performs similarly to virgin polypropylene and meets FDA standards for food-contact applications, enabling seamless integration into existing manufacturing processes.


Brand owners, foodservice operators, venues and converters interested in participating in circularity programs with PureCycle and WM are encouraged to contact PureCycle and WM.

**About PureCycle Technologies**


PureCycle Technologies LLC., a subsidiary of PureCycle Technologies, Inc., holds a global license for the only patented dissolution recycling technology, developed by The Procter & Gamble Company (P&G), that is designed to transform polypropylene plastic waste (designated as #5 plastic) into a continuously renewable resource. The unique purification process removes color, odor, and other impurities from #5 plastic waste resulting in our PureFive® resin that can be recycled and reused multiple times, changing our relationship with plastic.[www.purecycle.com](https://www.purecycle.com/)
